# Hypomagnesemia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Nephrology > Fluids, electrolytes, and acid-base disorders > Hypomagnesemia*

[Original Article Link](/library/sq0t-S)

---

## Summary

Hypomagnesemia (low serum <u>magnesium</u>) is very common in critically unwell patients but can occur in the community, particularly secondary to medication use. <u>Magnesium</u> has a vital role in membrane stabilization and while the symptoms of mild deficiency can be nonspecific, severe hypomagnesemia can cause serious complications, such as <u>cardiac arrhythmias</u> and <u>seizures</u>. Hypomagnesemia is commonly seen alongside other <u>electrolyte</u> abnormalities, and <u>magnesium</u> levels should always be checked in patients with <u>hypokalemia</u> or <u>hypocalcemia</u>. Management consists of <u>magnesium replacement</u>, treatment of associated <u>electrolyte</u> imbalances, and addressing the underlying causes.

## Clinical features

Low body <u>magnesium</u> stores can affect many organ systems. The presence and severity of symptoms do not always correlate with serum <u>magnesium</u> levels. [[2]](/library/bJYHsJ)




* Gastrointestinal: <u>anorexia</u>, <u>nausea</u>, <u>vomiting</u>

* Neuromuscular

* <u>Muscle weakness</u>, <u>lethargy</u>

* <u>Tremor</u>

* <u>Tetany</u>

* Muscle cramps, spontaneous <u>carpopedal spasm</u>

* <u>Hyperreflexia</u>

* <u>Paresthesia</u>

* Positive <u>Chvostek sign</u> and <u>Trousseau sign</u>

* <u>Ataxia</u>, <u>nystagmus</u>

* <u>Seizures</u>  [[4]](/library/vEYAxI)

* Cardiac [[5]](/library/HCdKtH0)

* <u>ECG</u> changes

* Prolonged <u>QT interval</u>

* Prolonged <u>p waves</u>

* Possibly <u>U waves</u>

* <u>Arrhythmias</u>

* <u>Torsades de pointes</u>

* <u>Supraventricular tachycardias</u>

* <u>Ventricular arrhythmias</u>

* <u>Atrial fibrillation</u>

* <u>Cardiac arrest</u>

* Metabolic disturbances

* Abnormalities of <u>calcium</u> metabolism

* <u>Hypocalcemia</u> (in severe hypomagnesemia)

* <u>Hypoparathyroidism</u>

* <u>PTH</u> resistance

* ↓ <u>Calcitriol</u> synthesis

* <u>Hypokalemia</u>

## Special patient groups

### Neonatal hypomagnesemia [[8]](/library/fYWkoP0)




* Definition: low serum <u>magnesium</u> levels in a <u>newborn</u>

* <u>Risk factors</u>

* <u>Maternal diabetes</u>

* <u>Prematurity</u>

* <u>Fetal growth restriction</u>

* <u>Hypocalcemia</u>

* <u>Hypoparathyroidism</u>

* <u>Renal tubular disorders</u> (e.g., <u>Gitelman syndrome</u>)

* Pathophysiology: maternal <u>hyperglycemia</u> → abnormal maternal <u>calcium</u>-<u>phosphorus</u> metabolism → ↑ maternal urinary Mg excretion → maternal hypomagnesemia → fetal hypomagnesemia → impaired <u>PTH</u> synthesis in the fetus → fetal <u>hypocalcemia</u> and hypomagnesemia

* Clinical features

* May be asymptomatic

* Gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., feeding intolerance)

* Neuromuscular symptoms (e.g., jitteriness, <u>seizures</u>)

* Respiratory symptoms (e.g., <u>apnea</u>)

* Diagnostics: serum <u>magnesium</u> level < 1.6 mg/dL

* Treatment: IV <u>magnesium</u> for symptomatic patients
